title: Power-generated ring maps induce universal homeomorphisms
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $p$ be a prime integer. Suppose $\ker\varphi$ consists of nilpotent elements and $B$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by elements $x$ each satisfying $x^{p^n}\in\varphi(R)$ and $p^n x\in\varphi(R)$ for some integer $n>0$ depending on $x$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. More explicitly, for every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$ the map $R'\to R'\otimes_R B$ satisfies the same two hypotheses (with the same prime $p$) and induces a homeomorphism on prime spectra.

proof.text: Put $A=\varphi(R)\subseteq B$ and let $T$ consist of the elements $b$ for which $b^{p^n},p^n b\in A$ for some $n>0$. Every element of $A$ is in $T$ (take $n=1$), so $0,1\in T$. If $x$ has exponent $n$, then $-x$ has the same exponent since $(-x)^{p^n}=(-1)^{p^n}x^{p^n}$. For $x,y$ with exponents $n,m$, $(xy)^{p^{n+m}}=(x^{p^n})^{p^m}(y^{p^m})^{p^n}\in A$ and $p^{n+m}xy=(p^nx)(p^my)\in A$. These verify additive inverses and multiplication without assuming characteristic $p$.

For $x,y\in T$, choose their positive exponents $n,m$ and apply [lem-pur-prime-power-addition-subring] to the subring $A\subseteq B$. It gives a positive $a$ with $(x+y)^{p^a},p^a(x+y)\in A$, hence $x+y\in T$. Together with step 1, $T$ is a subring containing $A$ and therefore an $R$-subalgebra. It contains every specified generator of $B$, so the meaning of generation as an algebra gives $T=B$.

For every $b\in B$, step 2 supplies the positive power $d=p^n>0$ with $b^d\in\varphi(R)$. The kernel hypothesis is exactly that every kernel element is nilpotent, with no uniform nilpotence exponent required. Apply [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] to obtain a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, in particular a surjection.

Fix an arbitrary commutative $R$-algebra $R'$ and put $B'=R'\otimes_R B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its spectrum map induced by $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$ is the base change of the surjection in step 3. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] makes $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ surjective. If $r'$ is in the kernel, every prime $\mathfrak p'$ of $R'$ is the contraction of a prime of $B'$ and hence contains $r'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] with $I=0$ in $R'$: the intersection of all primes is $\sqrt0$, whose elements have a positive power equal to zero. Consequently this kernel consists of nilpotents. This is deduced from spectrum surjectivity, not from tensor preserving injectivity.

Using the multiplication formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], the elements $1\otimes x$ for the original generators generate $B'$ as an $R'$-algebra: a tensor $r'\otimes b$ equals $(r'\otimes1)(1\otimes b)$, and express $b$ as a finite polynomial in the original generators and then sum the finitely many pure tensors. If $x^{p^n}=\varphi(r)$ and $p^nx=\varphi(s)$, balancing gives $(1\otimes x)^{p^n}=r'_0\otimes1$ and $p^n(1\otimes x)=s'_0\otimes1$, where $r'_0,s'_0$ are the images of $r,s$ in $R'$. Hence the same generator hypothesis holds with the same prime $p$ and the original exponents. Put $A'=\operatorname{im}(R'\to B')$ and $T'=\{b\in B': b^{p^n},p^nb\in A'\text{ for some }n>0\}$. The elements of $A'$ lie in $T'$ with $n=1$. For $u,v\in T'$ with witnesses $n,m$, the equalities $(-u)^{p^n}=(-1)^{p^n}u^{p^n}$, $p^n(-u)=-(p^nu)$, $(uv)^{p^{n+m}}=(u^{p^n})^{p^m}(v^{p^m})^{p^n}$ and $p^{n+m}uv=(p^nu)(p^mv)$ prove closure under negatives and products. Apply [lem-pur-prime-power-addition-subring] to $A'\subseteq B'$ to obtain closure under sums. Thus $T'$ is an $R'$-subalgebra containing the displayed generators, so $T'=B'$; every element has a positive power in $A'$. With the nil kernel from step 4, [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] gives the required homeomorphism on spectra.

For an arbitrary scheme $Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, cover $Y'$ by affine open subschemes $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the restriction of the pullback projection above $U_i$ is the spectrum map of $R_i\to R_i\otimes_R B$, and is a homeomorphism by step 5. Thus the projection is bijective: each target point has exactly one lift on any chart containing it. It is a homeomorphism globally: the inverse images of $U_i$ are open, and a subset of the source is open precisely when its intersections with these inverse images are open; their images are open in each $U_i$ and therefore open in $Y'$. By [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], this proves the universal-homeomorphism assertion for arbitrary scheme base changes, including the empty scheme.
